name: CoreWeave, Inc.
monetization: Rents Nvidia GPU capacity under multi-year take-or-pay contracts to Microsoft, OpenAI, and Meta; funds the fleet with ~$35B of largely GPU-collateralized debt.
description_md: CoreWeave is the largest independent neocloud: a crypto-miner-turned-AI-cloud that IPO'd in March 2025 and now operates one of the biggest Nvidia GPU fleets outside the hyperscalers. Its contracted backlog reached ~$129B at Q2 2026 (revenue backlog $104.2B as of June 30, +246% y/y, plus post-quarter signings) against quarterly revenue of $2.6B — an extreme ratio of committed-future to current revenue. Nvidia holds ~5% of CoreWeave and backstops $6.3B of capacity through 2032; customers are concentrated in Microsoft, OpenAI (~$22.4B of contracts), and Meta (~$35.2B). It leases most shells from third parties (Core Scientific, Applied Digital, Galaxy Digital) rather than owning them.
ai_monetization_md: GPU-hours under long-dated take-or-pay contracts: Microsoft (its original anchor tenant), OpenAI ($11.9B initial + expansions to ~$22.4B — roughly a third of contracted revenue when signed), Meta (~$35.2B through 2032), plus IBM, Mistral and enterprise AI labs. Q2-26 revenue was $2.575B (+112% y/y) with widening losses — net interest expense alone hit $640M in the quarter (2.4x y/y). The equity story rests on converting the $129B backlog at contracted margins; the credit story asks whether the debt stack that funds the GPUs amortizes faster than the GPUs depreciate. CoreWeave's own re-lease evidence (A100s contracted into 2029, H100s re-leasing near original rates) is the bulls' key datapoint on useful life.
ai_strategy_md: Scale ahead of the hyperscalers on Nvidia's newest silicon, financed by debt secured against GPUs and contracts (including the $7.6B GPU-backed DDTL 2.0 facility): total debt reached ~$35B at Q2-26 (from ~$30B earlier in 2026), plus >$10B of unsecured/convertible paper raised in Q2 alone, a $3.1B term loan, and a $1B strategic investment from Jane Street. Diversify the tenant base beyond Microsoft (OpenAI 2025, Meta 2025–26), acquire adjacencies (Weights & Biases ~$1.7B; the $9B Core Scientific merger was rejected by CORZ shareholders in Oct 2025, leaving CoreWeave leasing ~$10B+ from a landlord it failed to buy), and keep Nvidia alignment (equity, backstop, first-access to new architectures).
risk_notes_md: **Credit-market signal:** bond/CDS markets implied roughly a 50% 5-year default probability as of Jul 2026 (ANALYST-DERIVED from thin markets — confidence low; SPEC §10.4 caveat applies), and spreads widened ~125bp in Aug 2026 around earnings even as the backlog grew. **Leverage & duration mismatch:** ~$35B of debt against assets (GPUs) whose economic life and residual value are the sector's most contested numbers; collateralized_gpu_debt flag — collateral value correlates with the same demand cycle that drives revenue. **Customer concentration:** Microsoft, OpenAI and Meta dominate backlog; OpenAI is itself loss-making, and Meta/Microsoft have in-house alternatives — renewal risk lands exactly when refinancing is due. **Circularity:** Nvidia is supplier, ~5% shareholder, and $6.3B backstop counterparty. **Landlord dependence:** Core Scientific, Applied Digital (~$11B/400MW), Galaxy (>$30B potential Helios value) leases create fixed obligations senior to equity; guidance-vs-actuals discrepancies in FY26 remain a data-quality flag (SPEC §9.3).

observations.notes: Total contracted backlog incl. ~$29.6B signed in the ~6 weeks around quarter-end; formal revenue backlog $104.2B as of Jun 30, 2026 (+246% y/y, vs $30.1B a year earlier). Committed value, not revenue.
+112% y/y; losses widened, net interest expense $640M (vs $267M in Q2-25).
Includes GPU-backed facilities (e.g. $7.6B DDTL 2.0), >$10B of unsecured/convertible debt raised in Q2-26, and a $3.1B term loan. Earlier 2026 tallies were ~$30B — the stack grows quarterly.
